chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Her khul' (compensatory divorce) is not valid until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not fulfill a promise for you, and I will not obey you in a matter, and I will not perform ghusl for you from major ritual impurity, and I will lie on your bed (with another), and I will permit entry upon you without your permission.' And indeed, the people used to be lenient with what is less than this. So when the woman says this to her husband, it becomes permissible for him to take whatever he took from her. Thus, she remains with him having two remaining divorces left, and the khul' counts as one divorce.

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And the speech must come from her.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the matter were up to us, we would not validate a divorce except for the waiting period (iddah).'
ai.seo_question: What specific words must a wife say to make khul' valid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the precise verbal formula for khul', requiring the wife to explicitly declare her intent to endure specific inconveniences, thereby distinguishing it from simple mutual consent. It clarifies that khul' is legally counted as one irrevocable divorce, leaving the couple with two remaining talaqat, and notes the scholarly view that if authority rested solely with the Imams, divorce would only be valid after the waiting period (iddah).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Her Khul’a is not Permissible until she is saying to her husband, ‘By Allahazwj, I will not fulfill a promise for you, and I will not obey you in a matter, and I will not wash myself for you from the sexual impurity, and I will settle (another) on your bed, and permit upon you without your permission’, and the people used to permit with regards to what is less than this. So when the woman says said to her husband, it is permissible for him whatever he takes from her. So she would be with him upon two remaining divorces, and Al-Khul’a is one divorce’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the speech has to happen from her’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the matter was up to us<sup>asws</sup>, we<sup>asws</sup> would not allowed a divorce except for the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘Al-Khul‘ (divorce for payment) is not lawful until she says to her husband, “By Allah, I will not honor your turn, will not obey your order, will not take Ghusl (bath) for you because of sexual intercourse, will not sit on your furnishing and I will give permission without your permission.” People applied KhuV for less than that. The woman’s saying that to her husband makes it lawful for him to receive payment from her. She remains for him for two more divorces and al-Khul‘ is one divorce.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘The statements come from her.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Had the matter been in our hands we would not allow divorce except with waiting period.’”
